description: Sharpline dependency automation. CLAUDE.md section 12: 'Base images are pinned by digest, not by floating tag. Renovate or Dependabot proposes the bumps.'
Renovate PROPOSES; a human reviews and merges. Nothing here automerges, because a base-image digest bump is a reviewed change to the build substrate, not a rubber stamp.
Renovate itself runs as a hosted container against this repo, so it does not put a toolchain on any host and does not violate the prime directive.

schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: CLAUDE.md section 12: 'Base images are pinned by digest, not by floating tag.' This is the pinDigests policy itself - every container reference in a Dockerfile, a compose file or a Helm values file must carry an @sha256: digest, and Renovate opens the PR that adds one if a bare tag ever lands.
Container base images, version bumps. CLAUDE.md section 9 builds every service from a pinned base; moving them together keeps the compose stack and the Helm chart from drifting apart.

Digest-only movement. Nine of the fifteen pinned images resolve from a floating tag (:latest, :nonroot, :latest-pg17), so a digest bump is the ONLY update Renovate can offer for them. Re-resolving that tag returns a different digest; per the ledger that is a deliberate, reviewed bump and never a silent edit.
The `go` directive in go.mod must not drift ahead of the golang builder image, which the prime directive makes authoritative. Bump them in one PR or not at all.

The Playwright container tag must stay in lockstep with @playwright/test in web/package.json - a mismatch makes Playwright refuse to run (see 'Deviations from the requested tags' in the contract ledger). This rule sits after the generic image rules so it wins.
CLAUDE.md sections 7 and 9 mandate the node:24-alpine container. Host Node is editor tooling only and must never pull the image forward.
CLAUDE.md section 9 mandates caddy:2-alpine as the single entrypoint.
Go modules, non-breaking. One PR per week keeps `go test -race` signal attributable.
Go module majors land one at a time, behind dashboard approval. franz-go and pgx majors are the ones that will actually hurt.
franz-go is load-bearing: CLAUDE.md section 3 forbids confluent-kafka-go because cgo breaks CGO_ENABLED=0 and therefore the distroless image. Any franz-go change gets its own PR.
Frontend majors are dashboard-gated; a React or Tailwind major is a design-system event, not a dependency bump.
CLAUDE.md section 7: 'Next.js 15 (App Router). Not negotiable.' Hold the major until that line is amended.
GitHub Actions, pinned to commit SHAs. ci.yml and deploy.yml reference major tags today precisely so this rule can convert them.
Terraform providers and modules. CLAUDE.md section 9: Terraform owns the kind cluster, Kafka topics, Grafana dashboards and namespaces.
Python appears in exactly two places (CLAUDE.md section 2): Locust load tests and the analysis/ notebooks. Never in the serving path, so these can move together.
